channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Sign Energy Cooperation Roadmap for 2026-2028
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have signed a roadmap to expand energy cooperation for 2026-2028. Discussions covered renewable energy, a Central Asia-Azerbaijan green energy corridor, oil and gas exploration, and SOCAR's expansion in Uzbekistan.

item.title: New Greenhouse Initiative in Kegeyli Provides 50 Families with Stable Income
item.description: A new greenhouse complex in Kegeyli district, established with 12.5 billion soums in preferential funds, has created 50 jobs for families in the Social Register. Each family receives 10 acres of greenhouse space and two years of training to establish their own farms.

item.title: Uzbek President Visits Nukus Insulation Group, Inspects Modern European Equipment
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Nukus Insulation Group enterprise. The facility, valued at $50 million, is equipped with modern European machinery. This equipment enables the production of goods conforming to international standards using local raw materials.

item.title: Qoraqalpogʻiston Launches $7.6 Billion in Projects, Starts New Power Capacity Construction
item.description: Qoraqalpogʻiston has launched projects worth $7.6 billion and initiated the construction of new power capacities. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the ceremony. These initiatives are expected to create 8,000 high-paying jobs.

item.title: Samarkand to Host Global Summit on Child Well-being Investment
item.description: Samarkand will host the Global Summit 'Investing in Child Well-being: Towards Sustainable and Equitable Development for Future Generations' on October 21-22. The forum will gather leaders and experts from over 100 countries, including children and adolescents, to discuss social protection, health, and education.

item.title: New Poultry Farm in Kegeyli Boosts Regional Economy and Food Security
item.description: A new poultry enterprise, 'Kegeyli baraka naslli parrandа', with a $7.8 million investment, has created 70 jobs in Karakalpakstan. The facility can house 200,000 chickens and produces 27.5 million incubation eggs annually, contributing 4.8 billion soms to the local budget and enhancing food security.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Safe Labor Migration Opportunities to Japan, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Saudi Arabia
item.description: Uzbekistan is broadening safe labor migration routes, with citizens to be employed in Japan as drivers, Slovakia as forklift operators, Slovenia in service, and Saudi Arabia as nurses. The Migration Agency, in collaboration with other ministries, organizes training for in-demand professions and foreign languages.

item.title: Terrorist Attack in Karachi Mosque During Friday Prayer Kills 14, Injures Over 200
item.description: A suicide bombing occurred in a Shia mosque in Karachi during Friday prayers, killing 14 people and injuring over 200. The blast damaged the mosque, and investigators suspect a suicide bomber. Riots erupted in Karachi following the attack.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon to visit Sughd region, road closures expected
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon is scheduled to visit the Sughd region in the coming days. Authorities confirmed the visit but did not provide details. Traffic police announced road closures on September 20, 22, and 23 for security reasons. Some markets in Khujand will also be closed during this period.

item.title: Moscow Hotel Manager Sentenced to Three Years for Housing Crocus Attack Convicts
item.description: A Moscow hotel manager has been sentenced to three years in prison for providing accommodation to two individuals convicted in the Crocus attack. The court delivered the verdict, resulting in the manager's imprisonment.

item.title: Preventing Domestic Violence and Protecting Women's Rights is a Priority Task
item.description: A meeting in Shakhrinkhan district, Andijan region, focused on preventing domestic violence and protecting women's rights. Measures to support women, ensure their rights, and combat human trafficking were discussed. Emphasis was placed on supporting women with restraining orders.

item.title: Direct Flights to Launch Between Kulob, Tajikistan and Kazan, Russia
item.description: Direct flights will commence between Kulob, Tajikistan, and Kazan, Tatarstan (Russia), operated by Nordwind Airlines starting September 27. Flights will operate weekly, with tickets priced between 1600 and 2500 somoni one-way. The flights will use a Boeing 737-800 aircraft.

item.title: Kazakhstan Days of Medicine in Kyrgyzstan: 1,300 People Examined, Memoranda Signed
item.description: The Days of Kazakh Medicine in Kyrgyzstan concluded with 1,300 people examined and several memoranda signed. Leading specialists from both countries held joint operations, consultations, and master classes. Mobile medical complexes provided services in the Chuy region, examining 1,300 residents.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts SCO Meeting on Competition Policy Among Member States
item.description: Antimonopoly authorities from Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states convened in Dushanbe to discuss competition policy. Tajik officials highlighted the importance of fair competition and adapting policies to the digital economy. The meeting aimed to foster professional dialogue and experience exchange.

item.title: UN Report: Achieving Gender Equality Will Take Over 170 Years
item.description: A new UN report indicates that achieving gender equality at current rates will take 171 years. By 2030, none of the Sustainable Development Goal 5 targets will be met if progress doesn't accelerate. Issues include discrimination, violence, and unequal participation in politics and economics.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Asian Parliamentary Assembly Standing Committee Meeting
item.description: Dushanbe will host the next meeting of the Standing Committee on Social and Cultural Affairs of the Asian Parliamentary Assembly from September 24-27, 2026. The event, led by Tajikistan, will be the first APA meeting held in the country and aims to foster cooperation and promote sustainable development.

item.title: "Uzbekfilm" to Become Hub for Uzbekistan's Modern Film Industry
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva visited "Uzbekfilm" studio, emphasizing its transformation into a national brand and a hub for the modern film industry. The state's role will shift to a strategic partner, focusing on creating conditions and providing financial support, while private studios and producers will take the lead.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan discuss cooperation in training, employment, and investment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister met with the president of 'Onodera User Run' in Tokyo to discuss supporting employment projects for Uzbek citizens in Japan. They also explored creating new educational centers in Uzbekistan and expanding vocational training for youth. Uzbekistan and Japan aim to enhance cooperation in human capital development, employment, and investment.

item.title: Tajikistan discusses specialist training domestically and abroad
item.description: A meeting on specialist training in Tajikistan was held at the Ministry of Education and Science. Deputy Prime Minister Dilrabo Mansuri emphasized the importance of qualified personnel for socio-economic development. Discussions covered coordination, selection mechanisms for overseas study, priority training areas, and aligning specialties with national economic needs.

item.title: Migrant arrivals in Europe decrease, but sea route fatalities rise
item.description: The International Organization for Migration reported a 39 percent drop in migrant arrivals to Europe by sea. However, the number of deaths and disappearances on these routes has increased, with over 2,300 recorded so far this year. The central Mediterranean route saw the sharpest decline in arrivals but a rise in fatalities.

item.title: European Commission proposes banning social media for children under 13
item.description: The European Commission proposed the EU Kids Act to enhance online child safety, suggesting a ban on social media for children under 13. Those aged 13-15 could use 'mini-accounts' with parental controls. The act also imposes obligations on online services to prevent addictive features and limit screen time.

item.title: Tajikistan's Finance Minister discusses new financing mechanisms with Rothschild & Co
item.description: Tajikistan's Finance Minister met with a representative from Rothschild & Co in London to discuss cooperation on issuing government bonds and utilizing new financing mechanisms for priority projects. The meeting also focused on improving Tajikistan's international credit ratings and exploring prospects for bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer 30% Tuition Discount for Children of Educators
item.description: Starting from the 2026/2027 academic year, Uzbekistan will provide a 30% discount on tuition fees for children of educators enrolled in state higher education institutions. This applies to full-time undergraduate programs. The discount is not applicable to military, foreign, non-state institutions, or joint programs. Applications will be processed via the kontrakt.edu.uz system.

item.title: Tajikistan Responds to ICC on Failure to Arrest Vladimir Putin
item.description: The Tajik government has responded to the International Criminal Court (ICC) regarding its failure to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Tajikistan. The response details the reasons behind Tajikistan's decision not to detain Putin, despite the ICC's request.

item.title: Migrant Arrivals in Europe Decrease by 39%, While Fatalities Rise
item.description: The number of migrants arriving in Europe by sea has fallen by 39% this year, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Despite the decrease in arrivals, the number of deaths and disappearances at sea has increased. The Central Mediterranean route to Italy saw a 55% drop in arrivals but a rise in fatalities.

item.title: Tajikistan's Pamir petroglyphs and historical sites added to UNESCO tentative list
item.description: Five complexes of petroglyphs in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region have been included in UNESCO's tentative list. The Agency for Protection of Historical and Cultural Heritage stated these sites are valuable examples of Tajikistan's heritage with scientific, cultural, and historical significance.

item.title: UN mission finds US responsible for war crimes in Iran, Tehran for crimes against humanity
item.description: A UN mission found sufficient grounds to believe the US was behind two military strikes on an Iranian school and sports complex, deeming them war crimes. The mission also concluded Iran's government committed crimes against humanity during its violent crackdown on protests.

item.title: Karakol City Faces 80% Water Supply Cut Due to Pipeline Breakdown
item.description: Karakol city's drinking water supply is temporarily reduced by 80% following a breakdown in the central water pipeline, the City Hall reported. Repairs are underway, with restoration expected by evening.

item.title: China Ready to Deepen Cooperation with ASEAN in Digital Economy, AI, and Green Sectors
item.description: China is prepared to deepen cooperation with ASEAN in the digital economy, artificial intelligence, and green industries, stated Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang. He proposed focusing on enhancing openness, expanding trade, and strengthening supply chains.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Potato Cultivation
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Agricultural Sciences and China's 'For Future Tech Group' signed a memorandum of understanding to develop long-term cooperation in potato cultivation. The agreement includes scientific research, modern technology implementation, seed production, storage, processing, and marketing of potatoes, as well as joint investment projects.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Discuss New Infrastructure Projects and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a meeting on September 18, 2026, in Dushanbe to discuss economic cooperation, investment attraction, and industrial, energy, and transport sector collaboration. Special attention was given to developing production chains and implementing new water-energy and road-transport infrastructure projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Plans to Diversify Reserve Assets Beyond US Bonds
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank plans to gradually expand its reserve asset portfolio beyond US government bonds. As of early September, the bank held approximately 439 tons of gold, valued at nearly $65 billion, constituting about 90% of its international reserves.

item.title: Tajikistan's Water Resources Are Decreasing, According to WMO Report
item.description: Tajikistan's water resources are reportedly decreasing. A new World Meteorological Organization report indicates that water inflow into the country's reservoirs was below average in 2025. Further details are expected.

item.title: SCO trade ministers meet in Dushanbe to discuss economic cooperation and trade
item.description: Dushanbe hosted the 25th meeting of ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities of SCO member states on September 17, 2026. Tajik Minister of Economic Development and Trade Abdurahmonzoda Safarali chaired the meeting. Discussions focused on enhancing economic cooperation, increasing mutual trade, energy security, and investment.

item.title: Ombudsman's office helps children of labor migrants resume education in Batken region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman's office intervened to ensure three children of returning labor migrants could continue their education in Kyzyl-Kiya. The children were initially denied admission to a Russian-language school due to overcrowding. The Ombudsman's office contacted local authorities, and the children were subsequently placed in another school.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet head provides apartment to family of deceased rescuer
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's cabinet, Adylbek Kasymaliev, met with the wife of deceased EMERCOM lieutenant Askar Kazybekov, who died in the line of duty. Kasymaliev expressed condolences and assured the family of state support. Kazybekov was posthumously awarded the "Erdik" medal for bravery.

item.title: Schoolboy dies after fight between students in Kyrgyzstan's Suzak district
item.description: A 10th-grade student died from injuries sustained during a conflict with 11th-grade students in Zhygach-Korgon village, Suzak district. Two teenagers, aged 17 and 18, have been detained on suspicion of inflicting grievous bodily harm. A criminal case has been initiated, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: CIS exchange representatives discuss development of commodity and financial markets
item.description: Representatives from CIS countries' commodity and stock exchanges met in St. Petersburg to discuss the development of exchange commodity and financial markets. Key topics included the role of exchanges in economic regulation, principles for listing goods, and mutual access to securities. Discussions also covered digital financial assets and cooperation between national exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan develops 'kamikaze' drone with 1500 km range
item.description: Uzbekistan has developed a 'kamikaze' drone capable of flying up to 1500 km, presented as an alternative to the 'Shahed' drone. The drone, belonging to a private company, debuted at a defense technology exhibition in South Africa, where Uzbekistan is the sole participant from Central Asia showcasing various military products.

item.title: Schoolboy dies in Suzak district after conflict between 10th and 11th graders
item.description: A schoolboy has died in the village of Zhygach-Korgon, Suzak district, following a conflict between 10th and 11th-grade students. The 10th-grader sustained severe injuries and died en route to the hospital. Two teenagers have been detained.
